name: Information Bias
description: People may seek more information even when that information cannot improve the decision or change the action they should take. Knowing more feels useful or reassuring even when it is instrumentally irrelevant.
design_relevance_note: Relevant to dashboard bloat, filter creep, explainability panes, consent settings, and research workflows where teams gather more data that cannot actually change the next action. More information is not always better if it only adds certainty theater.
prevalence_note: Known in medical/diagnostic decision research and occasionally very useful in product-research or settings-design critique, but rarely named explicitly in mainstream UX pattern libraries.

findings.description: In diagnostic-reasoning problems, people sought or valued extra information even when it could not change the decision they should make, revealing a bias toward information and certainty for their own sake rather than for instrumental usefulness.
findings.source_title: Heuristics and biases in diagnostic reasoning: II. Congruence, information, and certainty
findings.source_venue: Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes
